clue.text: Alliance head: 'Keir's first to go!'

indicators.note: something told to go must leave, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: block is slang for a person's head, as in 'knock your block off'

indicators.note: the first of a name is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of Keir

explanation.surface: A political alliance's leader cries that Keir Starmer must be ousted first.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove K from BLOCK to leave BLOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of countries or parties combined for a common political purpose.

clue.text: Feeling elected court bears up fools

indicators.note: in a down clue the court carries the next piece on top of it, so that piece is written first

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: nits is British slang for idiots
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A sensation that the elected court is propping up a bunch of idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an intuitive sense of something, a gut reaction rather than reasoned thought.

clue.text: See 28
Feature of a forest's warning device light

parts.note: a car horn is sounded as a warning
a beam is a shaft of light

explanation.surface: A forest is equipped with an alarm that flashes a light.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbeam is a hardwood tree, so it is one of the trees found growing in woodland.

clue.text: They smoke a lot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: chimneys, which give out smoke

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests heavy smokers; the first half is factory chimneys instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimney stacks emit smoke, and informally having stacks of something means having plenty of it.

clue.text: British, these cold spreads that cover kippers

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'things that cover kippers', a plural noun

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: spreads suggests letters being scattered about and laid out anew in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some British cold spreads that are laid over smoked herring at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Kippers here are not smoked fish but people who kip, a British word for sleeping; spreads also hints at bedspreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and blankets are laid over people sleeping in bed, keeping sleepers warm through the night.

clue.text: Glorious, glorious leader from an earlier age

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever stands at its front, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of glorious
olden means belonging to former times, as in 'the olden days'

explanation.surface: Praise for a magnificent ruler of a bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: Glorious appears twice: once as the definition, once as the source of a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden age or golden moment is a splendid, magnificent one, so the adjective means glorious.

clue.text: Doctor, what's that you said about crush?

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the joined letters are read backwards

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
eh is the noise made when asking someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A patient asks the doctor to repeat what was said about their infatuation.
explanation.walkthrough: Crush looks like a romantic infatuation, but here it is a tightly packed crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A crush is a dense mass of people, and a herd is a large throng, especially one moving together.

clue.text: Fish having round tongue

parts.note: the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fish with a rounded tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue in the sense of a language; lingo is an informal word for a language or jargon.

clue.text: Mobile home, not, unfortunately, very close to lake

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters before it are put into a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the comma
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of lake

explanation.surface: A mobile home that is, sadly, not quite near the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Mobile home reads as one item, a caravan, but the definition stops at Mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mobile is moving about or travelling, which is exactly what this idiom describes.

clue.text: Quite unresponsive, Tom needs a restorative

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written
a tonic is a medicine that restores strength

explanation.surface: Tom has gone completely unresponsive and needs a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is in a stupor, motionless and not reacting to anything around them.

clue.text: Was a programmer from Delaware into fish?

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up inside it, enclosed by the second

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware

explanation.surface: Asks whether a software developer from Delaware was keen on fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmers write software instructions, so having done so means having written computer code.

clue.text: Depressed old fellow clutching jerry can

indicators.note: to clutch something is to hold it tightly, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: cove is an old British slang word for a man or chap

indicators.note: jerry-built means shoddily put together, so the next word is assembled badly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy old man hanging on to a fuel canister.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerry can reads as one thing, a petrol container, but jerry is the shuffle signal for can.
explanation.definitionFit: A depressed surface is sunk inward, which is what a concave shape is: curved in like a bowl.

clue.text: Large group that flies by day

parts.note: a crow is a bird, something that flies
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A swarm of insects that is active in the daytime.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a large number of people gathered together in one place.

clue.text: Disturbing repercussion of dessert wine

parts.note: afters is British informal for pudding, the course after the main one
hock is a British name for German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: The unsettling consequence of drinking a sweet pudding wine.
explanation.definitionFit: After an earthquake comes a smaller tremor, and figuratively an unsettling consequence of some event.

clue.text: Backfiring jokes about how to be humiliated

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed surrounding the other
something backfiring goes off the wrong way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: puns are jokes on words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Jokes that misfire are a reliable way to embarrass yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shown up is to be embarrassed by being exposed as inferior in front of others.

clue.text: Smooth out papers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to iron flat, as with clothes
second meaning: newspapers collectively, the media

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to flatten some documents, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb means to iron creases away, and the noun covers newspapers and journalists generally.

clue.text: Players shivering, etc in zero temperature

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
shivering letters tremble and shake out of place into a fresh order

parts.note: zero is written like the letter O
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Musicians and others are shivering in sub-zero cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight musicians performing together, so its members are players.

clue.text: Almost fail to return for Mass

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards
almost all of something stops just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to bomb is to fail badly, as a show that flops

explanation.surface: Someone nearly misses going back to church for Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like the church service, but here it means a great crowd of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob is a disorderly crowd, and the masses are the general populace in large numbers.

clue.text: Note the possible risks of webcast with a nerd

indicators.note: cast means thrown, and letters thrown about land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the front of webcast
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch out for the dangers of an online broadcast hosted by a geek.
explanation.walkthrough: The signal is hidden inside webcast: web is fodder, cast tells you to rearrange it along with a nerd.
explanation.definitionFit: This set phrase is a warning, telling someone to take notice of the dangers ahead.

clue.text: Army store reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a hoard is a stockpile or store

explanation.surface: A military supply depot has been mentioned in dispatches.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a vast crowd, originally a nomadic tribe or band of warriors, hence an army.

clue.text: Men are unlikely leading chemical testers

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the rearranged piece comes before the other
unlikely suggests something improbable or out of order, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
gents is short for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Men are not expected to be the frontrunners in chemistry tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagents are substances added to a sample to detect or measure other substances by reaction.

clue.text: Kalahari's flies?

definitions.note: an example of the plural answer, read as 'Kalahari is one of these'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: arid sandy regions, the Kalahari in southern Africa being one
second meaning: runs away, abandons a post

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a question about insects in the Kalahari; the question mark warns that the first part is defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is an arid region of southern Africa, and to flee or abscond is to abandon one's post.

clue.text: Celeb on Viagra initially needs energy fast!

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning, so just the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Viagra
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A celebrity on Viagra urgently needs a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast looks like an adverb meaning quickly; it is the verb meaning to go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without food deliberately is to abstain from eating, which in the extreme means going hungry.

clue.text: Brightened up by books aimed at tabloid readers?

indicators.note: writing aimed at a readership is labelled with that readership's name in front

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, standing for its own readers here
lit is short for literature

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered up by books written for the mass-market press audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful idea of literature written for readers of The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brightened is lit up, and a place illuminated by daylight is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Knowing Charlie's an insolent American

parts.note: wise means knowing, informed
a charlie is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie, savvy but cheeky, is described as a rude American.
explanation.definitionFit: This US slang term names someone who makes smart, impertinent remarks, a cheeky know-it-all.

clue.text: Showy floor wood

parts.note: FL is the abbreviation for floor
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A flashy floor made of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal flash means ostentatious and expensive-looking, designed to impress people.

clue.text: Establish nothing's left to finance

indicators.note: having left means having gone away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to found an institution is to establish it
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Setting up a business when there's no money left to pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O out of FOUND to leave FUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund a project is to provide money for it, paying its costs.

clue.text: City's name Rex inscribed in fancy beer mug

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: a name inscribed in something is written into it, so one letter goes inside
fancy describes something elaborate, so the letters after it are reworked into an elaborate new order

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as on coins

explanation.surface: A king's name has been engraved on an ornate stein.
explanation.walkthrough: The beer mug fits the Bavarian city, home to a famous Christmas market.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuremberg is a large city in Bavaria, southern Germany.

clue.text: Brummie's shot crooked landlord!

parts.note: Brummie is the setter, so the setter's means belonging to me

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of true, so the letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Birmingham man has gunned down a dishonest landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham; here it is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for the setter himself.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned jocular phrase names the landlord of a pub or inn, who hosts the drinkers.

clue.text: Go north of the border for party

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Scots verb for to go, Scotland being north of the English border
second meaning: a group of people working or going around together

explanation.surface: Head up to Scotland for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the verb means walk or go, and as a noun it means a band of people.

clue.text: After a month, oxygen added to Michael's anaesthetic

indicators.note: added to means attached on, so the pieces are simply joined together

parts.note: NOV is the abbreviation for November
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
Michael Caine is the English film actor

explanation.surface: After a month, Michael's painkiller has been topped up with oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Novocaine is a trade name for procaine, a local numbing drug used by dentists.

clue.text: Unacceptable lament of batsman out on 99?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British idiom for something not allowed or out of order
second meaning: in cricket a ton is a hundred runs, so one short means missing the century

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ton is a century, a hundred runs; a batsman dismissed on 99 might cry that there is no ton, splitting the letters differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something just isn't done means it is improper; the regrouped letters give the batsman's complaint.
